messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Perceived depression scores improved significantly more in the TRI 360TM multi-ingredient supplement group than in the placebo group.
Sentence: "All assessed perception scorings on psychological symptoms like fatigue, mental stress, sleep disturbance, anxiety, depression, emotional trauma, mood changes, self-confidence, willpower, and motivation were very significantly (p ≤ 0.0001) improved in TRI 360TM participants than placebo control group."
Measured as: depression perception scoring
Population: Adults aged 20-45 years with one or more psychological symptoms
Intervention: TRI 360TM proprietary nutraceutical combination capsules twice a day, up to 180 days
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 84
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation did not reduce Hamilton D-17 depression scores compared with placebo at 12 weeks in patients with depression.
Sentence: "No significant reduction in depression was seen after vitamin D supplementation compared to placebo at Hamilton (18.4-18.0; p = 0.73 at 12 weeks)."
Measured as: Hamilton D-17 depression score
Population: Outpatients aged 18-65 with mild to severe depression
Intervention: Vitamin D3 70 micrograms daily on top of standard treatment
Comparator: Placebo on top of standard treatment
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A tests a multi-ingredient nutraceutical (vitamin D not identified as the active exposure) in adults with psychological symptoms, while Study B tests vitamin D3 alone in depressed outpatients; the two results point different ways, with population, intervention and outcome measure all differing.","verdict":"genuine","reason":"intervention","also_differs":["population","outcome_measure"],"detail":"multi-ingredient TRI 360TM combination vs vitamin D3 70 mcg daily alone; self-perceived depression score vs clinician-rated Hamilton D-17"}
